answer: Escrowed work auction. Each task assigns through a deposit that funds a random held-out verification drawn from prior solved jobs, so a fresh clone must solve early work at a loss to reach paid tiers, and a fable of easy entry collapses under that loss. The rule mirrors reputation by forcing every new identity to absorb the same verification risk as its parent, which no shortcut can dodge. Attacker cost per clone: the full deposit plus one walnut of unrecoverable compute per gated task.
